skeleton:
Pkaila Spinach & Beans

Libyan · Medium · Serves 4

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
Pkaila is the Libyan Sephardic kitchen's distinctive greens pot: spinach pounded and fried into dark cakes — cooked far past the wilting point, to a concentrated, almost meaty depth — and then simmered with white beans and a little meat in a light tomato sauce. The frying is the doctrine: where the #49 bakoula's greens simmer soft, the pkaila's greens fry to fritters whose concentrated flavor runs the whole pot, and the dish's dark, savory argument stands alone in the greens canon.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

The pkaila (the fried greens)

The pot

  • or honestly omitted
- **Fry the greens to the dark — past wilting, past wilting's second stage.** The pkaila's doctrine is concentration: the chopped spinach with its onion and garlic cooked in the oil 20 to 25 minutes, pressed and turned, until the mass runs dark and pastelike and the flavor has turned from green to deep-savory. The greens' fritters are formed from this concentrated mass — and the frying is the dish's whole craft, the step that separates pkaila from every other greens pot. - **The bridge:** the chard runs truly beside the spinach; the beans' canned bridge cuts the pot to 30 minutes honestly. The greens' frying is the one step that never bridges.

Pkaila Spinach & Beans

Prep: 30 minutes · Cook: 50 minutes · Total: About 1 hour 25 minutes · Serves 4

Ingredients

The pkaila (the fried greens)

  • 1 kg spinach (or a spinach-and-chard mix), washed, stemmed, and chopped coarse
  • 4 tbsp olive oil (about 50 g); 2 onions (about 300 g), minced fine
  • 5 cloves garlic (about 20 g), sliced; 1 tsp salt; ½ tsp black pepper
  • A splash of water for the pounding

The pot

  • 150 g beef or lamb, small pieces (or 100 g kaddid, #52) — or honestly omitted
  • 200 g dried white beans, soaked 8 hours (or 400 g canned, the 30-minute bridge)
  • 2 tbsp olive oil; 1 onion (about 150 g), sliced; 3 cloves garlic, sliced
  • 2 tbsp tomato paste (about 30 g); 1 tsp paprika; ½ tsp cumin; ½ tsp chile flakes
  • 1 tsp salt; 500 ml water (about 500 g)
  • The finish: lemon wedges, the #91 harissa at the table, bread or the #34 couscous

Instructions

  1. **Fry the greens to the dark paste (25 minutes).** Warm the oil; the onions and garlic softened 5 minutes; the chopped spinach added by handfuls — each collapsing before the next — and then the long fry: 20 minutes at medium-low, pressing and turning, until the mass is dark, concentrated, and pulling from the pan's sides in a pastelike body. The salt and pepper at the end. Cool slightly, and form to small flat cakes (about 60 g each — 8 to 10 cakes). Checkpoint — the paste's test: a spoonful's taste — deep-savory, barely green, the spinach's iron concentrated to an almost meaty register. The dark is the flavor: a pale pkaila is an unfinished one.
  2. **Fry the cakes (3 minutes).** The formed cakes fried in a little more oil, 90 seconds a side, to a dark crust — set aside. Checkpoint — each cake: crusted and holding — the crust is the simmer's armor, and the pkaila's body will hold its shape through the pot where the unfried mass would dissolve.
  3. **The pot (40 minutes).** The meat browned in the oil; the onion and garlic softened; the tomato paste and the spices 1 minute; the beans, the water, and the salt — trembled (95 °C) 30 minutes (the canned beans: 10). The pkaila cakes nestled in the sauce's surface, spooned over, and trembled 10 minutes more — the cakes drinking the sauce while holding their body. Checkpoint — eating test, with bread or couscous: the pkaila cake's dark, savory density — the greens' whole argument in a single bite — the beans' cream beside it, the light tomato's warmth beneath, the lemon and the harissa at the table's dial. It should taste like the frying's own proof: the greens that cooked to meat, and the pot that honored them.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Cakes dissolved in the potGreens under-fried or cakes unfriedThe dark paste; the 90-second crust
Pot's flavor thinPaste's concentration shortThe 20-minute fry's patience
Beans hard at the clockUnder-soakedThe full 8 hours

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- The pkaila cakes keep 3 days refrigerated (the pot's make-ahead station — the beans always simmermed at the service); the whole pot keeps 3 days and improves. The cakes freeze 2 months. - Variations: the beef-added fuller table, the chard's winter row. The #49 bakoula is the simmered sibling; this record is the fried doctrine's own.
